producer.composed_of: 752 instances + 1046 effects/projectiles in the last frame

motion_proof.note: two frames read 1.2 s apart from one live ring

what_this_shows: A window with the real draw path (meshes, shadows, MSAA) can render frames decoded from a ring written by a running GameManager, with interpolation between frames.
Latency gate in the unit it was written in: at draw time the picture is 0 producer frames old at the median and p95, 1 frame at p99 (limit 2).
Decode of a full 752-instance frame costs 0.76 ms median inside the consumer.
The ring's content changes while it is consumed: two reads 1.2 s apart differ in 96 ship positions and in effect count (1,118 -> 1,058).
what_this_does_not_show: Not a frame rate: the producer is limited by the Python simulation (125 ms median tick on this stress fixture), not by the bridge, so the stream runs at ~4.9 Hz.

The 1.0 ms serialization budget is met for instances-only frames (0.55/0.71 ms) but NOT for the live composition (752 instances + 1046 effects/projectiles): 2.37 ms median. Listed as the next optimization target rather than hidden.
No fog, HUD, planets, transients drawn, or gameplay input in the window.
Player visibility set is not computed here (all frames are all-visible); wiring the renderer's own visibility set is the live-integration step.
Nothing tested on Windows/D3D12; CI remains disabled by the owner.
